claimAdjudications.ruling: UPHELD, and strengthened beyond what the author offered.
evidence: Three-way canonical-JSON comparison, all byte-identical at sha256 d5eab95c0678968f434c46573d757679452ff18fc6df08ee488196bca5bb07ca (137,617 bytes, 34 top-level keys): (A) my own independent resolver, (B) check-completeness.py resolve_derivation, (C) check-c2-v9.py apply_derivation.

Import independence CONFIRMED: check-completeness.py imports only copy, hashlib, json, pathlib, re, sys. It does not import check-c2-v9.py, and check-c2-v9.py does not import it. Neither loads the other through its exec/importlib sites.

HOWEVER the author's two-implementation cross-validation is weaker than it reads, because the path-step grammar is a VERBATIM textual copy: both files define the identical regex \[(\d+)\]|\.?([^.\[\]]+) (check-completeness.py STEP_RE line 107; check-c2-v9.py _STEP_RE line 3181). A defect in that shared grammar would be replicated in both and the cross-validation would not catch it. The instrument's comment is candid that this is deliberate, but the agreement it buys is correspondingly narrower than 'two independent implementations agree'.

I closed that gap myself: my resolver (A) parses paths with a hand-written splitter and compares with its own type-exact equality function, sharing no code with either. It agrees byte-for-byte. The cross-validation therefore stands on genuinely independent footing after this review, which it did not before.

claimAdjudications.claim: 6. The selftest's own rigour / the two surviving mutants
claimAdjudications.ruling: SPLIT. The equivalence argument for the two survivors is SOUND. The characterisation of the suite as '12 killed, 2 survivors' materially UNDERSTATES its gaps.

twoSurvivorsAdjudication.ruling: EQUIVALENT on all reachable inputs -- not a defect. Keep the deepcopies anyway.
reasoning: A1 (effective = base instead of deepcopy): `base` is produced by json.loads(raw) freshly inside every resolve_derivation call, and in the chained case by a recursive call that itself returns a freshly built document. json.loads never shares objects between calls. After apply_operations returns, the caller never reads `base` again. I could construct no input where mutating it in place is observable.

A2 (aliasing op['value']): JSON parsing creates a distinct object per literal, so no two operations in one document can share a value object. A later operation writing INTO an earlier operation's added value does mutate the declaration in place -- I built that case (add newBlock {count:1}, then set newBlock.count) -- but the declaration is discarded with the artifact at the end of contract_shape and is never re-read, so it too is unobservable.
Both survive my battery for the same reason the author gives, and I accept the argument.
twoSurvivorsAdjudication.qualification: The equivalence is CONTINGENT, not local. It holds only because (a) load_bytes returns immutable bytes and parsing is repeated per resolution, and (b) the effective document is scored and dropped. Memoising the loader or caching parsed predecessors -- an obvious optimisation on a 372-document corpus -- would silently turn A1 into a live cross-contamination bug in which one surface's resolution corrupts another's. The deepcopies are the cheap guard that makes the property local instead of emergent. Removing them would be safe today and unsafe after a change nobody would think to connect to it.

theOpenQuestionTheAuthorLeft.answer: BOTH ARE SUBSTANTIALLY INSTRUMENT ARTIFACTS, NOT ARTIFACT DEFECTS. I resolved this; the author left it open.
theOpenQuestionTheAuthorLeft.RUST-PROVIDER-PROTOCOL: Missing only the goldens point. It DOES carry goldens: 6 `semanticConformanceVectors`, each with id / kind / initialState / event / guard / actions / expected / falsifies -- unambiguously golden cases with expected outcomes. theOpenQuestionTheAuthorLeft.TRUSTED-REQUEST-CONTEXT: Missing both the schema and the goldens point, and both appear to be naming artifacts. The 2/4 is the weakest figure in the table and is probably the least accurate one.
theOpenQuestionTheAuthorLeft.consequence: Contract shape 11/13 should be read as a FLOOR. At least two of the remaining shortfalls are instrument blindness, not missing contract. nonBlockingObservations.title: The selftest is materially weaker than the author's account of it
nonBlockingObservations.detail: Reported as 14 mutants / 12 killed / 2 equivalent survivors. I ran 17 and 11 survived. Every one of my 9 new survivors is test debt rather than a live defect -- I exercised each shipped branch directly and all behave correctly -- but the suite does not pin: the whole chain-recursion path (recursion, cycle guard, DERIVATION_MAX_DEPTH, non-object predecessor), full-digest comparison as opposed to prefix comparison, `set` missing its `from`, empty operations arrays, list-index paths, or the declaration_fields partial-declaration error branch. Since this instrument's output is quoted into a signature-bound record, unpinned guards are the ones a later edit removes silently. Suggested minimum: one delta-of-delta fixture, one cycle fixture, one fixture whose declared digest shares a long prefix, and one single-block two-filename fixture.

nonBlockingObservations.title: The two surviving mutants are equivalent only by grace of the caller
nonBlockingObservations.detail: Accepted as equivalent. But the property depends on load_bytes returning immutable bytes and on re-parsing per resolution. Any future memoisation of loading or parsing converts A1 into cross-surface contamination. The deepcopies should stay, and the reason should be a comment at the deepcopy rather than an argument in a review.

nonBlockingObservations.title: A detection false positive exists and the design is right anyway
nonBlockingObservations.detail: An artifact carrying an RFC-6902 JSON Patch (which uses exactly `op` and `path`) beside one .json filename and one sha256 in the same object fires the detector. The corpus contains zero such documents today. I want to record explicitly that NARROWING is_operation_list to the declared verbs would be the WRONG fix: detection must stay broader than acceptance, otherwise a derivation with an undeclared verb would cease to be detected at all and would fall back to own-key scoring silently -- destroying the unknown-verb gate. Detect broadly, refuse loudly is correct.

nonBlockingObservations.title: `operations: []` is the one malformed declaration that degrades silently
nonBlockingObservations.detail: is_operation_list requires a non-empty list, so a declaration with an empty operations array is not recognised as a declaration at all. The document is scored on its own keys with NO finding. This is the single exception to the instrument's stated 'it NEVER degrades silently'. It fails in the safe direction (understates, cannot manufacture a point) and check-c2-v9.py independently rejects an empty operations array as a finding, so nothing is currently exposed -- but the prose is absolute where the behaviour is not.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Predecessor integrity is verified; predecessor AUTHORITY is not
nonBlockingObservations.detail: Nothing constrains WHICH file an artifact may declare as its predecessor. I built a 'parasite' with no schema and no goldens of its own that inherited a 4/4 from an unrelated document by declaring it with a correct digest. This is NOT a new weakness and NOT a blocker: exploiting it requires editing the binding artifact, and the pre-existing name predicate is strictly easier to forge -- score_document awards both schema and goldens to {"xSchema": {}, "xFixtures": [1]}, i.e. for an empty object and a one-element list, on key names alone. The derivation path at minimum demands a real file, a matching sha256 and type-exact `from` restatements. It raises the bar rather than lowering it. Worth recording only because the inherited content is no longer visible in the file a human opens, which is precisely why the printed provenance block (predecessor, both digests, schema keys, per-array golden counts) is load-bearing and must not be dropped.

whatIDidNotCheck: I did not verify the substantive CORRECTNESS of v4's stageSchemas as a contract, nor of the 113 fixtures as test cases. I established that they exist, that they are structurally real (closed kinds, required/optional/effectClass, prohibition list; fixtures with valid/invalid flags), that they are untouched by the 13 operations, and that they are counted correctly. Contract shape is a PRESENCE measure everywhere in this instrument -- the name-based path awards the same point for an empty object under a matching key -- so I held the derivation path to presence, not to correctness.

I did not re-derive any of check-c2-v9.py's internal measurement work: not the 440,495-case path-injectivity attack, not jx_canon, not the guard inventory, not the skeleton digest. I used exactly one function from it, apply_derivation, and only as a comparison oracle.
I did not re-run check-c2-v4.py's selftest matrix over the predecessor.

I did not audit the instrument's non-derivation halves beyond running them -- review_state, resolution_state, finding_ids, unregistered_current_reviews and the cross-cutting path were exercised by --selftest and by the live run, but I wrote no mutants against them. My mutation work was confined to the derivation reader.
I did not attempt a sha256 near-collision to make the M8 prefix mutant reachable in practice; I established only that the shipped code compares digests in full.

I did not verify the 12 name-scored surfaces' binding artifacts beyond applying the shape predicate and, for the two below 4/4, inspecting their top-level keys. In particular I did not sweep the other ten for renamed or nested contract sections, so the count of surfaces whose shape figure is depressed by CMP-IR-01's rename/nesting half may be higher than the two I identified.

I did not test the instrument under concurrent modification of an artifact between processes. I did confirm that within a single resolution the bytes hashed and the bytes parsed are the same object, so no window exists inside the reader itself.
I did not evaluate whether contract shape, as a four-point presence measure, is the right instrument for gating seal readiness at all. That is a design question above this review.
I did not read IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md in full. I read the CMP-IR-01 row, the §3 figure block and the §9.1 figure block, and grepped for the quoted numbers.
scope: Independent review evidence only. Nothing here is signed, sealed, frozen, applied or integrated. No finding is closed, no disposition is softened, no status is changed. CD-RT-5 remains BLOCKED_ON_PHASE_1A. This review does not authorise adoption of the instrument and does not reconcile the freeze's stale figures -- it establishes only that the movement those figures must be reconciled TO is earned and correctly attributed. All probe work was performed on a copy of the tree under a private scratchpad; the only file I wrote under docs/coop/ is this one.
